subject: step function with confidence interval shaded

messages.author: 20048bbfd3d3908b
messages.subject: step function with confidence interval shaded
parts:
Hi - What is a good way of plotting a step function with upper/lower
bounds shaded (as in geom_smooth, for example)?

For example, I can plot:

x <- 1:10
df <- data.frame(x=x, y=x+10, ymin=x+7, ymax=x+12)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_step()
p + geom_step(aes(x, ymin, linetype=2), data=df) + geom_step(aes(x,
ymax, linetype=2), data=df)
print(p)

How would I shade the area between ymin and ymax?

At first I thought I would experiment with geom_ribbon or geom_smooth
in conjunction with stat_step. But it seems there's no such object
"stat_step" even though google turns up some references in a
"changelog". (I'm using ggplot2 0.8.5)

Aside, I only started learning ggplot2 recently and everything they
say is really true: it's very cool!

Thanks much for any help!

Despite the changelog entry, there doesn't seem to be a stat_step.
There is a stairstep function, but it makes a lot of assumptions.
This is a cobbled together approach; it transforms the data.frame
using a variant of the stairstep function, and then plots using that
transformed data.frame. "Ugly hack" might be a generous description.
Better, more elegant solutions welcome; a real stat_step very welcome.

stairstep.name <- function(df, direction, x.name, y.name) {
df[["x"]] <- df[[x.name]]
df[["y"]] <- df[[y.name]]
ss <- stairstep(df, direction=direction)
ret.df <- data.frame(ss[["x"]],ss[["y"]])
names(ret.df) <- c(x.name, y.name)
rownames(ret.df) <- rownames(ss)
ret.df
}

step.df <- Reduce(merge,alply(setdiff(names(df),"x"), 1, function(y)
{stairstep.name(df, "hv", "x", y)}))

ggplot(step.df, aes(x,y)) + geom_smooth(aes(ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax),
stat="identity")

--Brian Diggs

On Mar 17, 8:48 pm, wcyee <wcy...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Oh wow, thanks Brian!

> doing.  :)  And then perhaps modify it to work with a factor variable
> in my frame to draw two step curves with confidence bands.

I suppose a comment or two wouldn't have hurt :)

ggplot2::stairstep takes a data.frame and a direction and transforms
the "x" and "y" columns, copying the other ones. stairstep.name is a
wrapper around this function which takes a data.frame, direction, and
the name of the two columns to transform. It basically makes a
data.frame renaming the columns as "x" and "y", does the
transformation, and renames them back.

The Reduce... line does this transformation for "x" paired with every
other variable in the data.frame, and then merges them back together.
This gives a data.frame with the supplementary points that when
connected give the stepping. This data.frame can then be used
directly with geom_smooth().

--Brian Diggs

Sorry to revive a dead thread, but it comes up high when searching for step ribbons. I constructed a stat_stepribbon function that seems to be working well for me that answers your desire for a "stat_step" for ribbons. ("stat_step" would seem to be logical for lines, but there is already a perfectly functional geom_step that works fine for that purpose.)

See this thread: https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/ggplot2/9cFWHaH1CPs
